supporting: closures as a context for enclosing scopes

claims.claim: Python resolves an unqualified name by searching local, enclosing-function, module-global, then built-in scopes when those scopes apply.
A binding operation anywhere in a function block makes that name local throughout that block unless a global or nonlocal statement changes that treatment.
Using a local name before it has been bound in a function raises UnboundLocalError, a subclass of NameError.
A global statement directs references and assignments for its listed names to the module's global namespace.
A nonlocal statement refers to a previously bound name in the nearest enclosing function scope; without a suitable enclosing binding it is a compile-time SyntaxError.
A nested function can retain access to an enclosing function's names, which makes enclosing scope relevant to closures.
